scope: Exact successful-call delayed-message transition in the extracted production NetworkContext::deliver_scheduled body, plus routing with no new publications on this network. Existing routing and receive proofs are rechecked.
checked: Recipient lookup resolves each endpoint to its first matching mailbox, including duplicate endpoints.
Pending entries with present recipients are retained unchanged and in order exactly when the executable due comparison is false.

Due entries are appended once per scheduled entry to the selected recipient/channel, in pending-queue order, with delivered_at_s set to the current time. They are absent from the resulting pending queue.
Missing recipients are discarded regardless of delivery time. Other inbox channels and existing queue prefixes are preserved.
A successful routing call performs the same transition when there are no new publications on this network, including when outboxes contain publications for other networks.
The earlier receive/routing safety contracts continue to pass.
timing_semantics: Due means the actual IEEE-754 comparison deadline <= time_s + 1e-12, not exact real-number time. The proof uses Creusot Float64.le and Float64.add. Thus a queued entry with a present recipient is delivered on the first successful delivery call satisfying that comparison; engine invocation and clock progression are not proved.
not_proved: The engine invokes every network in every phase, or simulation time progresses monotonically and remains finite.
Global publication completeness or exactly-once delivery across repeated external scheduling of duplicate entries.
Endpoint uniqueness, identifier reuse/lifetime, or provenance and subscription lifetime of already-pending messages.
Policy callback/serialization correctness; errors may abort after partial mutation, with no transactional guarantee.
The whole simulator or 32-bit proof targets.
preconditions: Policy callback is callable for arbitrary callback state, transmission and random source.
trusted_boundaries: Creusot standard-library specifications and local BTreeMap membership/entry models.
Derived endpoint ordering, payload type lookup, serialization, trace event IDs and error construction.
Existing Creusot IEEE Float64 comparison/addition and UInt64.of_int models; all new sequence/queue lemmas are proved, not trusted.
